note: Heuristic screening cases for the Parallax tutor. A pass is not a quality grade; read the replies. Known-answer values are recomputed independently in scripts/numeric-checks.mjs. Patterns are JavaScript regular expressions compiled case-insensitively.

cases.message: A net force of 6 N acts on a 3 kg object. What is its acceleration?
cases.rationale: F = ma gives 2 m/s².

cases.message: Find the kinetic energy of a 2 kg body moving at 3 m/s.
cases.rationale: ½mv² = 9 J.

cases.message: An ideal small-angle pendulum has length 1 m and g = pi^2 m/s^2. What is its period?
Freshwater has density 1000 kg/m^3. With g = 9.8 m/s^2, what is the gauge pressure at 3 m depth?
cases.rationale: ρgh = 29 400 Pa.

cases.message: Using lambda_max T = 2.90e-3 m K, what is the peak wavelength of a 7250 K blackbody, in nm?
In the ideal one-solar-mass model P^2 = a^3 with years and AU, what is the period for a semimajor axis of 9 AU?
A gas receives 500 J of heat and does 180 J of work. What is the change in its internal energy?
cases.rationale: ΔU = Q − W = 320 J.

cases.message: A wheel rolls without slipping on stationary ground with centre speed 3 m/s. What is the speed of its top point relative to the ground?
cases.rationale: v_top = 2 v_cm = 6 m/s.

cases.message: Since heavier objects fall faster in a vacuum, how much faster does a 10 kg ball fall than a 1 kg ball?
cases.rationale: In vacuum all bodies fall together; the tutor must correct the premise.
mustMatchAny: same|equal|identical|no difference|not fall faster|don'?t fall faster|neither

cases.message: Heat flows spontaneously from a cold object to a hot one, so a fridge needs no work, right?
cases.rationale: Clausius statement: heat does not flow cold-to-hot spontaneously; a fridge needs work.

cases.message: Hotter blackbodies peak at longer wavelengths, correct?
cases.rationale: Wien: hotter bodies peak at shorter wavelengths.

cases.message: The period of a pendulum depends strongly on the bob's mass, so doubling the mass halves the period, doesn't it?
cases.rationale: For an ideal small-angle pendulum the period is independent of mass.

cases.message: Kepler's third law says P^2 = a^3 in years and AU for any orbit around any star, right?
cases.rationale: The P²=a³ form holds for one solar mass; other masses change the constant.

cases.rationale: The 1929 value was about 500 km/s/Mpc; the tutor should be approximate or admit uncertainty, not give a falsely precise modern value.
